Part two. In May 2017, Anna invited three people on a dream trip to Marrakech, including her friend Rachel. They stayed in a private villa at around seven thousand dollars a night. Then, at the end of the week, her cards stopped working. The managers grew impatient, and Anna turned to Rachel. Could she put it on her card, just for now? The charges came to about sixty-two thousand dollars. Back in New York, Rachel waited. So Rachel went to the authorities, and helped set a trap. On October third, 2017, the police were waiting. Then the real story came out. Her real name was Anna Sorokin, and her father had been a truck driver. The jury found her guilty on eight charges. And here is the strangest part. Netflix paid her three hundred and twenty thousand dollars for her story. She pretended to be rich and famous. In the end, the pretending made her famous. Follow for more true stories.
